title: There Will Never Be Another You

analysis.notes: A bebop favourite because every phrase is a ii–V into somewhere: a minor ii–V–i into Cm (Dm7b5–G7–Cm7), a ii–V into Ab (Bbm7–Eb7–Abmaj7), a backdoor dominant (Db7, the bVII7) sliding home to Ebmaj7, then the home ii–V (Fm7–Bb7) with a iii–VI–ii–V chain in the last eight. Learn to hear each ii–V's target and the tune plays itself.

learning.why: The graduation tune: three key centres, minor and major ii–Vs, a backdoor dominant, and a bright tempo. It is on every session list and everything in it appears in a hundred other standards.
drills: Comp shells at 120 BPM naming the target key of each ii–V aloud as it passes.
Loop bars 9–11 and play Ab major then the Db7's Ab melodic-minor sound into Eb.
Solo with guide tones only at 168 BPM, then add chromatic approaches.
Turn on the ii–V–I x-ray and comp only the ii–V units, resting on the I chords.
listen: Sonny Stitt — Sonny Stitt Sits In with the Oscar Peterson Trio (1959)
milestones: Know the form and changes from memory
Comp shells through the form without looking
Comp drop-2 voicings with the trio at 168 BPM
Play a chord-tone solo over the whole form
Play the melody from memory (learn it by ear from a recording)
